newsitem.title: UK: Israeli offical says Hebron differences "settled".
newsitem.headline: Israeli offical says Hebron differences "settled".

text.p: Israeli Deputy Prime Minister Moshe Katsav said on Monday that stumbling blocks which have delayed a handover of the West Bank holy city of Hebron to Palestinian control have been removed.
"We (Israel) believe all differences are settled already. We have no differences with the Hebron situation," he told a news conference in London.

"If (Palestinian President) Yasser Arafat says "yes' we will sign tomorrow," Katsav, who is also Israel's minister of tourism, told reporters at the launch of an initiative to encourage tourism to Israel.
Katsav declined to comment on press speculation that a deal on the withdrawl of Israeli troops from Hebron could be signed by the end of the week.
Earlier on Monday, Israel Radio said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu hoped for a deal before he left on Wednesday for a planned week-long visit to the United States.
Israeli concern for the security of Jews in Hebron has held up its handover to Palestinian self-rule. Some 400 Jews live and study there amidst 100,000 Arabs.
Palestinian officials had hoped to clinch a deal on the long-delayed Israeli troop pullback during a Middle East economic conference starting on Tuesday in Cairo.
But on Monday, PLO officials said they did not expect a breakthrough at the two-day conference following a phone call on Sunday between Netanyahu and Arafat.

"Netanyahu called Arafat last night and he reiterated his commitment to implementing the deals, but as far as we are concerned this is only a verbal commitment," Palestinian peace negotiator Hassan Asfour told Reuters.
"It is not translated in the talks and they do not give it to us on paper," Asfour said.

Katsav also said Israel would like to withdraw its troops from southern Lebanon "as soon as possible" but that any withdrawl would be conditional on Lebanese authorities taking responsibility for law and order in the area.
"It is in our interest to withdraw," Katsav said. "We have no intention to remain in south Lebanon."
